    ELISA quantification from a standard curve

    Source: R/bio-assays.R
    bio_elisa_quant.Rd

    Fits a four-parameter logistic standard curve to the wells with known concentrations and back-calculates the concentration of every well from its response. Wells whose response lies outside the fitted asymptotes cannot be quantified and get NA with in_range = FALSE. Unknowns are flagged as extrapolated when their estimate falls outside the range of the standards.

    Usage

    bio_elisa_quant(
  .data,
  response,
  concentration,
  .by = NULL,
  dilution = NULL,
  level = 0.95
)

    Arguments

    .data

    A data frame or tibble with one row per well.

    response

    <tidy-select> Measured signal (for example optical density).

    concentration

    <tidy-select> Known concentration for standards and NA for unknown samples.

    .by

    <tidy-select> Optional columns defining separate plates or runs, each with its own standard curve.

    dilution

    <tidy-select> Optional column of dilution factors; estimates are multiplied by it.

    level

    Confidence level for the curve parameters.

    Value

    A <bio_assay> holding .data plus estimated_conc (after dilution correction), in_range, extrapolated and is_standard. The standard curves are kept for tidy(), glance() and autoplot().

    References

    Findlay, J. W. A. and Dillard, R. F. (2007). Appropriate calibration curve fitting in ligand binding assays. The AAPS Journal, 9, E260-E267. doi:10.1208/aapsj0902029

    Examples

    # Run 1 of the DNase ELISA as the standard curve; unknowns from run 2
plate <- rbind(
  transform(subset(dnase_elisa, run == 1), known = conc),
  transform(subset(dnase_elisa, run == 2), known = NA)
)
quant <- bio_elisa_quant(plate, density, known)
quant[!quant$is_standard, c("conc", "density", "estimated_conc")]
